Subject: Re: Draft MSA/DPA/SOW for Redwood integration — initial legal flags

Team / Evan —

I reviewed the MSA/DPA at a high level. Key items we need to address before we can sign:

MSA (priority):
- Indemnity: BlueGlow's broad indemnity for third-party claims is acceptable, but we need a reciprocal carveout for misuse by end customers of combined products.
- Liability cap: propose mutual cap at the higher of USD 2M or 2x fees in the first 12 months; current draft lists unlimited cap in a number of edge sections that we must narrow.
- Confidentiality: tighten carveouts for aggregated telemetry (we want explicit language that aggregated, de-identified metrics may be used by either party).

DPA (priority):
- Subprocessor list & notification: require 30 days notice before onboarding new subprocessors; right to object for restricted customers.
- Data residency: BlueGlow should confirm where data will be stored; if EU customer data involved, we need SCCs or equivalent.
- Audit rights: limit audits to once per 12 months and to a mutually agreed scope; require remediation window.

SOW (operational):
- Payment schedule: move 40% on signing, 40% on staging acceptance, 20% on live GA. Current draft milestones are front-loaded differently.
- Acceptance criteria: need explicit performance/LATENCY targets for pilot (p50/p95) and rollback clauses.

I attached a redline with inline comments (redline_MSA_LB_20260911.docx). Evan — please have your counsel review the liability and subprocessor language in particular; we can be flexible on payment milestones if operational acceptance criteria are firm.

—Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference
attachments: redline_MSA_LB_20260911.docx (docx)
